key_insight: KNIGHT combines topic-specific knowledge graphs with LLM-based generation to produce multiple-choice question datasets with controllable difficulty, enabling fast, grounded assessment data creation.
problem_solved: Reduces the time, cost, and effort of building specialized MCQ evaluation datasets for LLMs and RAG systems, while addressing difficulty control and factual grounding from external sources.
method: Construct a parsimonious, topic-specific knowledge graph from external sources to capture entities and relations as a structured summary.
Use LLMs to generate MCQ components (stems, correct answers, distractors) grounded in the knowledge graph to ensure factual consistency.
Apply adaptive hardness calibration to tune distractor quality and question difficulty, producing datasets with controllable difficulty distributions.
impact: Allows AI/ML practitioners to rapidly create grounded, difficulty-calibrated MCQ benchmarks for model evaluation and RAG testing, lowering evaluation bottlenecks and improving reproducibility.

paper_title: KNIGHT: Knowledge Graph-Driven Multiple-Choice Question Generation with Adaptive Hardness Calibration
paper_authors: Mohammad Amanlou, Erfan Shafiee Moghaddam, Yasaman Amou Jafari, Mahdi Noori, Farhan Farsi
